entities.name: Daśaratha

T: Aged; Rāma is the son of his old age (Bāla 19)
Sixty thousand years since his birth — an epic idiom for great age, not a literal figure to render
On hearing the request he is seized by great fear and lurches from his seat (18.20: ⟨Bāla 18.20, GRETIL — text withheld⟩).
For a moment he is as if senseless, then recovers and speaks (19.1: ⟨Bāla 19.1, GRETIL — text withheld⟩).
I: Aged — Rāma is the son of his old age (source).
Dress: uncut draped handloom, never tailored (material world).
Ornament: from the relief vocabulary; no European regalia (material world). Specific pieces: production design.
S: His tell: the right hand on the carved armrest. It closes before he speaks.
From film 3: stepped down from the dais, palms joined.

evidence.for: uncut draped cloth, its weight and fall
evidence.note: court panels — the best record of how a drape actually moves on a seated figure
2nd c. BCE — the earliest clear ornament vocabulary on royal bodies

evidence.for: how a king sits and who sits where
skin modelling and palette under lamp

entities.name: Viśvāmitra

T: An ascetic under an observance that prevents him cursing his attackers (Bāla 18)
Of the line of Kuśika; called Kauśika and Gādhi's son
At the king's promise he is thrilled — hair standing on end (18.1: hṛṣṭaromā).
At the refusal he is seized by wrath (20.1 samanyuḥ; 20.4 roṣaparīta); the whole earth shakes and fear enters the gods (20.4).
Tr: Iconographic traditions show matted hair and a staff
I: An ascetic under an observance (source).
Dress: uncut, undyed or ochre, draped (material world).
Specific appearance: production design.
S: A plain wooden staff, worn at the base, no carving, no finial.
He sits and does not move through four films. That stillness is the performance.

evidence.for: forest hermitage rather than wandering mendicant
matted hair, ash, bare torso, single cloth

never: VILLAIN CODING of any kind — narrowed eyes, shadowed face, low menacing angle

entities.name: Rāma

T: Not yet sixteen — AS HIS FATHER SAYS IT (Bāla 19). A character's statement, never narrator fact.
kākapakṣadhara — wearing the boy's side-locks — at the moment he is asked for (Bāla 18). The clearest signal that he is a child.
The spine elsewhere uses a term for his colour. NOT LOCATED. No complexion may be presented as source-mandated.
Tr: Tulsīdās: ⟨Tulsīdās, Rāmcaritmānas — text withheld, see SRC.TULSI⟩ — the two brothers, dark and fair. Tradition, not text.
I: A boy, not yet sixteen as his father says it (source).
Wears the boy's side-locks — kākapakṣadhara, 18.8 and 21.6 (source).
Carries a bow at the departure — dhanvī, 21.6 (source).
Complexion: not established by the source; production design governs. Never presented as source-mandated.
S: First appearance is film 7, on the road — plain medium, eye level, no light finding him.

evidence.for: a visible contrast between the brothers
evidence.note: śyāma and gaura. Tradition's contrast, not a spine mandate. Supports difference without asserting a sourced complexion.

evidence.for: a boy's body and bearing at fifteen

never: a man's body on a boy's role
blue skin — a much later iconographic convention

entities.name: Lakṣmaṇa

T: Sumitrā's son. Named by matronymic at the departure (Bāla 21).
I: Sumitrā's son; follows Rāma (source).
Dress: uncut, draped, plain (material world).
S: Half a step behind Rāma, always. The order is fixed by the source.
He watches Rāma more than he watches the road.
He does not speak in this arc. His attention is the performance.

evidence.for: the fixed walking order and the archer's guard

never: his own heroic beat in Bāla
a separate colour palette from Rāma

I: Near Rāma; a gentler bearing.
S: In Ayodhyā he wears what a man wears who is ruling from outside the city — plain, unadorned.

I: With Bharata, always.

T: She performs the rite at the aśvamedha and passes a night with the horse (Bāla 13).
I: Eldest queen. Older, composed. Fine dyed cotton with a border, restrained gold.
S: Grief held in, never performed.

evidence.for: queen's dress register, border, ornament count

entities.name: Kaikeyī

I: Youngest queen.
S: In Bāla she is simply a queen.

never: pre-loading Ayodhyā's villainy into a Bāla frame
harder features than the other queens — the oldest and laziest visual lie in every screen Rāmāyaṇa

I: Middle queen. Quiet presence.

T: Family priest of the Raghus. He counsels the king to keep his word (Bāla 20).
I: Family priest of the Raghus (source).
Brahmin dress: undyed, draped; the sacred thread (material world).
S: Among the ministers, frame-right and deeper, in films 1–4.
Rises once, in film 5, and the whole room registers it.
Speaks once, in film 6. That is the arc's turn.

evidence.for: brahmin dress, thread, restraint of ornament
he counsels the king to keep his word

T: Eighth minister; charioteer.
I: Older, capable, plain dress — a man who drives.
S: In Ayodhyā he returns with an empty chariot. That is his whole performance.

T: Eight ministers, named (Bāla 7).
I: Eight to twelve men; cream and undyed antarīya, dark shawls; a range of ages, builds and complexions; oiled bound hair; minimal ornament.
S: Seated on the floor or low stools — no chairs with backs. They react once per film, never more.

evidence.for: how many, at what density, doing what
evidence.note: crowd panels — the corrective to a wall of extras facing camera

T: Vibhāṇḍaka's son, forest-raised, who has never seen a woman (Bāla 9).
I: Young, unworldly, bark cloth.

T: Daughter of Daśaratha's line, given to Ṛśyaśṛṅga.
Janaka's priest; he tells Rāma Viśvāmitra's history in arc 13.
S: Middle-aged brahmin, seated, a narrator's stillness.

T: King of Mithilā; keeper of the bow; Sītā's father.
I: A king with a scholar's bearing — Mithilā is known for it.

T: Janaka's daughter, found in a furrow.
S: Human and specific. NO divine radiance.

entities.name: Tāṭakā

T: A yakṣī with the strength of a thousand elephants (Bāla 23); Sunda's wife, Mārīca's mother; cursed by Agastya.

evidence.for: she is SHOWN to them on the road, not an ambush

never: using her form to justify the killing

entities.name: Mārīca & Subāhu

T: They break the rite and defile the altar (Bāla 18); incited by Rāvaṇa (Bāla 19.18).

entities.gate: DO NOT DEPICT in Bāla 18–22. Named in two films, seen in neither.

entities.name: Rāvaṇa

T: Of the Paulastya line; brother of Vaiśravaṇa; son of Viśravas; holds a boon from Brahmā (Bāla 19).

entities.gate: DO NOT DEPICT in Bāla. No silhouette, no shadow, no hand, no throne, no Laṅkā. The room widening on the name is the whole effect.

entities.name: Mantharā
never: ugliness as moral signal — that reading is tradition and television, not a fact to render

T: Arrives with an axe on the road home (Bāla 15).
S: Heavy, used, unglamorous — the axe and the man both.

T: The poet. The krauñca birds, the hunter, the first śloka (Bāla 2).
S: The only figure who may be shown writing or reciting.

T: On the Sarayū; founded by Manu; twelve yojanas long; broad well-laid highways, watered and strewn with flowers; gates and bolts; shops in rows; theatres, gardens, mango groves; a moat (Bāla 5–6).
I: Timber and plaster over brick. Packed earth streets. Water tanks. Gardens within walls. A rammed-earth and brick wall with timber gates.
S: Prosperous, ordinary, alive — not a golden fantasy skyline.

evidence.note: Bāla 5–6 — length, highways, moat, shops, gardens. Rare specificity; follow it.

T: The spine describes NONE of this. Every line below is inference or staging, declared.
I: Timber posts and carved beams; mud-brick and lime plaster; worn sandstone floor; post-and-lintel throughout.
High pierced lattice openings on one side.
Brass oil lamps on stands; undyed unpatterned drapes.
S: Light enters from frame-left, always. The hall runs away from camera to a low dais.

evidence.for: interior colour, lamps, drapes, painted plaster
evidence.note: our palette reference — if a grade cannot sit beside an Ajanta plate it is wrong

entities.name: The gate of Ayodhyā

I: Timber leaves, twice the height of a man, in a rammed-earth and brick wall.
Iron strap hinges and a drawbar. No arch of later vocabulary — a flat lintel of heavy beam.
The road outside is packed earth, rutted by carts, not paved.
Bharhut and Sanchi show exactly this: gateway as post-and-lintel timber, rendered in stone.
S: Opened inward, by two men, without ceremony.
It is a gate, not a monument. Nothing about the shot should announce a departure.
Afternoon light, the sun lower in the west.

evidence.note: 2nd c. BCE railings — timber vocabulary in stone

never: anything that makes leaving look grand

T: They reach its bank at the departure (Bāla 21).
I: Wide, shallow, sandy banks, earth ghats, timber boats.

S: Afternoon light, the sun lower in the west.

entities.name: Tāṭakā's forest

T: Once the prosperous countries of Malada and Karūṣa; ruined by her (Bāla 23).
Loud with cicadas; big cats, boar, elephants; dhava, aśvakarṇa, bilva, tinduka, pāṭala, badarī trees.
S: Thorn, bare branch, hard shadow, dust. Silent rather than lush.

evidence.note: Bāla 23 — dhava, aśvakarṇa, bilva, tinduka, pāṭala, badarī; cicadas

never: anything that reads as fantasy wilderness

T: Vāmana's former hermitage (Bāla 28).
I: A clearing, thatched huts, a brick fire altar, cattle, students.
Wide, shallow, sandy banks, earth ghats, timber boats.

S: Must read as a DIFFERENT place from Ayodhyā — different timber, different plaster colour, different light.

I: Rock, river, green shade.
Deep forest; a built hut.
Low teak seat, knee height — this world sits near the floor, not on a dais chair.
Carved armrests with gold leaf worn thin where hands have rested for forty years.
A single sandstone step, not a pedestal.
Amarāvatī court panels show the geometry: the seated king barely above those around him.
S: Deep red cloth over the seat, the same red as his uttarīya.
Occupied in films 1–2. EMPTY from film 3 onward, and never re-occupied.
The empty seat is a character in films 3–6. Frame it as one.

evidence.for: seat height, armrest form, court geometry

I: Plain dark wood — dense, close-grained, the kind cut from a hard tree and kept.
Shoulder height on a tall man. Worn pale and smooth at the grip.
The base is blunt and splayed from years of being set down on stone.
No carving, no binding, no finial. An ascetic's staff is a walking stick that has walked.
S: Planted at his right through films 1–4. It does not move.
Raised once, in film 5, and set down on sandstone — the only percussive sound in the arc.
In the strike frame it is the only thing in focus.

evidence.for: how a standing figure holds it

I: Standing lamp, shallow oil dish, single wick, small flame.

evidence.for: form and how its light falls

S: One plain gold band, right hand — the continuity anchor in every hand detail.

I: Recurved Indian form, wood and horn, unstrung at rest.

T: Kept by Janaka; no one can string it (Bāla 30).
S: Enormous, ancient, covered, on a wheeled chest. Its WEIGHT is the point, not its decoration.

T: Golden, silver-lidded, carried by a being that rises from the fire (Bāla 15).
Released for a year; returns (Bāla 13).
S: An animal, garlanded. Not a spectacle.
Heavy, used, unglamorous.

I: Plain wood.

T: Twenty-one posts of bilva, khadira, palāśa, śleṣmātaka and devadāru; eight-angled, smoothed, wrapped in cloth, garlanded (Bāla 13).
